headline: Feature parity with the macOS Console
items: The Tube Modeller gives each output the character of one of 16 popular vacuum tubes, with drive, mix and an output stage that recreates how a valve amplifier's transformer meets a loudspeaker. Find it in the menu under Tube Modeller (Ctrl+Shift+D).

Every output has its own brickwall limiter with adjustable threshold and release. Click the icon under an output's mute button to switch it on, or right-click it for settings. Linked outputs share their limiter settings.

A spectrum analyser shows the sound on any input or output as it plays: behind the response graph, as bars under it, and in its own window (Ctrl+Shift+A). The device does the measuring, so it works with every source.
The Subharmonic Synthesizer adds a new octave below the bass, for recordings that are light on low end (Ctrl+Shift+S).

Filters can be edited directly on the response graph. Drag a band's dot to change its frequency and gain, scroll to change its width, and use the card beside it to pick a shape. The graph can also show phase.
Control Surfaces wire buttons, knobs, encoders, LEDs, an IR remote and a small display to spare GPIOs, with channel groups, macros and auxiliary outputs. Find them in Settings under Control.
Console now carries the matching firmware and installs it for you from Firmware Update in the menu. If a connected device runs a different version, a banner offers the update.
A setup wizard on first launch walks you through installing DSPi on a Pico. You can skip it, and run it again from Help in the menu.
Device configurations can be exported and imported as .dspipreset files shared with the macOS and Windows Consoles, and filters as REW or AutoEQ text.
The Signal Generator, Stats for Nerds and Interrupt Monitor have been rebuilt, and Settings has been redesigned to match the rest of the app.
